items.description: One named presentation clock: a tick clock, whose phase advances with the simulation's engine tick through a period, or a state clock, whose phase is the fractional part of a state row's presented value (an advancing row wraps once per unit). A projection carries a state clock as an anchored clock instead, whose phase its recipient predicts from the anchor at the tick it presents (WorldClockAnchor); a document never authors one.

name.description: The clock's name, unique within the section.

periodSeconds.description: A tick clock's period, in seconds: a whole number of engine ticks (1/50400 s). Refused beside State.

spanSeconds.description: What one period reads as, in the units a key's time is authored in: a day that passes in twenty minutes and reads as twenty-four hours has a span of 24h. Absent reads as the period for a tick clock and as one for a state clock.

startSeconds.description: How far into its span a tick clock stands at engine tick zero, in SpanSeconds' units, in [0, span). Absent is zero. Refused on a state clock.

state.description: A state clock's Fixed or Int row. Refused beside PeriodSeconds.

anchor.description: An anchored clock's anchor: what a projection carries for a state clock it discloses, in place of the row. Refused in an authored document. An anchored clock carrying none reads no phase, as the state clock it stands for reads none while its row holds no number.

tick.description: The engine tick the anchor stands at.

phase.description: The phase at Tick, a whole turn being 2^64.

rate.description: The phase one authoritative tick adds, wrapping; zero for a clock held still.

step.description: The engine ticks one authoritative tick spans; zero exactly when Rate is.

anchor.title: WorldClockAnchor
